name: AMD Radeon Pro VII product page (archived AMD page) - FP16/FP32/FP64/INT8 figures, dense, no structured-sparsity label
publisher: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD page, retrieved via the Wayback Machine)
notes:
READ 2026-10-04 via web_extract for the express purpose of establishing the AMD structured-sparsity convention on this record, because accelerators/amd-radeon-pro-vii currently carries only an fp32 row and cites this page.

NEGATIVE FINDING, VERBATIM-IN-EFFECT: the rendered page as extracted contains NO TFLOPS figure, NO 'Peak ... Performance' specification row, and no sparsity footnote. A regex sweep for 'sparsit', 'TFLOPS', 'TFLOP', 'TOPS' and 'Peak ' over the full extracted text of 18,346 characters returned ZERO matches. I am therefore recording that this page did not yield a usable compute figure on this pass rather than inventing one.

SPARSITY CONVENTION: nothing can be stated because the page carries no compute row at all. It is NOT evidence that the stored fp32 13.1 TFLOPS is dense or sparse; it is simply silent. Per this repo's standing rule that a figure needs a document, the fp32 13.1 TFLOPS row in accelerators/amd-radeon-pro-vii REMAINS UNSOURCED on the vendor side after this pass. The number is widely attributed to AMD (Radeon Pro VII = Vega 20 with 7.4 TFLOPs FP64 and correspondingly 14.8 FP32 / 29.5 FP16 by the Vega-20 ratio, which does not match 13.1), so its provenance should be treated as unestablished.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: AMD's Radeon Pro VII datasheet PDF (the same /system/files/documents/ path pattern as the MI50 and MI60 sheets) is the document to look for. It was not located on this pass; the Wayback capture used here is of the product page, not a datasheet PDF.
